subject.title: feat(imessage): native poll controls for approval prompts

question: Should capable iMessage bridge installations automatically prefer native approval polls, with reactions and text commands retained only as fallbacks?
rationale: This is a user-visible default behavior change for an existing approval workflow. The contributor’s stated direction and proof are strong, but maintainer intent is needed before accepting the default interaction and the associated authority boundary.

options.title: Approve capability-gated native polls
options.body: Accept native polls as the default only when the bridge advertises the required capability, while preserving all existing fallback controls.

options.title: Retain reaction-first behavior
options.body: Keep tapback controls as the default and treat native polls as a future opt-in or separately designed interaction.

recommendation.title: Approve capability-gated native polls
recommendation.body: Accept native polls as the default only when the bridge advertises the required capability, while preserving all existing fallback controls.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged channel-policy work and the branch’s approval-boundary hardening connect this owner most directly to the delegated-context and Gateway-resolution contract.
